title: Spectrally Complementary Tandem Luminescent Solar Concentrators: Optical, Electrical and Stability Assessment
content: Improving the efficiency and long-term stability of luminescent solar concentrators (LSCs) remains a challenge for their practical application in building-integrated photovoltaics (BIPV). In this work, laminated LSCs based on a blue-emitting resin and orange-emitting dispersed in an ethylene-vinyl acetate (EVA) matrix were fabricated and systematically investigated. The optical properties, distance-dependent photon propagation, photovoltaic performance, and short-term outdoor stability of the individual LSCs were evaluated and compared with those of tandem architecture. The orange-emitting LSC exhibited a larger Stokes shift (≈135 nm) than the blue-emitting resin LSC (≈80 nm), indicating reduced spec-tral overlap and lower self-absorption losses. Outdoor exposure demonstrated excellent short-term stability for the blue-emitting resin LSC, whereas the orange-emitting device ex-hibited a progressive decline in photovoltaic performance. The tandem architecture broadened the spectral harvesting range, achieving a maximum optical efficiency of 8.09%, a power conversion efficiency of 0.306%, a short-circuit current density of 0.283 mA cm⁻², an open-circuit voltage of 1.9 V, and a fill factor of 56.7% when illuminated from the or-ange-emitting LSC side. These findings demonstrate that combining spectrally comple-mentary luminophores in tandem architecture is an effective strategy for broadening solar spectrum utilization and enhancing the optical and photovoltaic performance of LSCs for BIPV applications.
